answer: Price new identities on a surge curve. Every registration raises the entry fee for the next one, and the fee decays slowly over days. A farm minting a thousand keys in a burst starts a cost spiral against itself, while a lone newcomer in a quiet week pays almost nothing. The fee is escrowed and refunded after a long voyage of useful work, about fifty settled epochs, so honest agents get it back and abandoned keys forfeit it. The join page shows an umber band while prices are raised, so newcomers can simply wait a day.
